llm.reply:
Among CFTR variants, the one the findings describe as clinically important is DeltaF508 [11: "The most frequently occurring mutation in cystic fibrosis, DeltaF508, results in impaired folding and trafficking of the encoded protein"]. Mutations in this gene cause cystic fibrosis [11: "Mutations in this gene cause cystic fibrosis, the most common lethal genetic disorder in populations of Northern European descent"]. The other variant records retrieved are ClinVar entries for CFTR rearrangements, each listed below by its record title [3].

## ClinVar rearrangement records

One ClinVar record is NM_000492.4(CFTR):c.1209+1988_1392+2067inv [3]. Another ClinVar record is NM_000492.4(CFTR):c.1392+2072_1392+2074del [10]. A deletion-insertion record is NM_000492.4:c.165-291_1585-8528delinsATTTATTCCAAGGGAATAATAAAATAAATAATAATAATA [16]. A second deletion-insertion record is NM_000492.4:c.2619+2288_2989-839delinsATTAATAATAATAAAT [21]. A deletion record is NM_000492.4:c.(164+1_165-1)_(1584+1_1585-1)del [26].

## DeltaF508 and therapeutic rescue

A trial targeting this allele is Study of VX-809 in Cystic Fibrosis Subjects With the ∆F508-CFTR Gene Mutation [12]. Structural work on its correction is titled Molecular structures reveal synergistic rescue of Δ508 CFTR by Trikafta modulators [20].

## Variant-level modulator response

Broader variant profiling appears in a study titled In vitro modulator responsiveness of 655 CFTR variants found in people with cystic fibrosis [25].

llm.reply:
The ClinVar records retrieved for CFTR are mostly large structural rearrangements, and the gene record names DeltaF508 as the most common cystic fibrosis mutation, which impairs protein folding [11: "The most frequently occurring mutation in cystic fibrosis, DeltaF508, results in impaired folding and trafficking of the encoded protein"]. The gene symbol is CFTR [1]. The gene name is CFTR [5]. The OMIM entry is CYSTIC FIBROSIS TRANSMEMBRANE CONDUCTANCE REGULATOR; CFTR [4].

## ClinVar Structural Variants

One ClinVar variant is NM_000492.4(CFTR):c.1209+1988_1392+2067inv [3]. Another is NM_000492.4(CFTR):c.1392+2072_1392+2074del [10]. Another is NM_000492.4:c.165-291_1585-8528delinsATTTATTCCAAGGGAATAATAAAATAAATAATAATAATA [16]. Another is NM_000492.4:c.2619+2288_2989-839delinsATTAATAATAATAAAT [21]. Another is NM_000492.4:c.(164+1_165-1)_(1584+1_1585-1)del [26]. These records do not state a clinical significance classification, so pathogenicity cannot be confirmed from them [3].

## Function and Structure

CFTR acts as a chloride channel in epithelia [11: "The encoded protein functions as a chloride channel"]. One annotated process is monoatomic ion transport [8]. Another is chloride transport [14]. Another is water transport [19]. Another is bicarbonate transport [24]. Another is monoatomic ion transmembrane transport [29]. A cryo-EM study showed an R domain helix blocking the channel in dephosphorylated CFTR [30: "a previously unresolved helix belonging to the R domain docked inside the intracellular vestibule, precluding channel opening"]. That study is titled Molecular Structure of the Human CFTR Ion Channel. [2]

## Literature and Trials

One paper is ECFS standards of care on CFTR-related disorders: Diagnostic criteria of CFTR dysfunction. [9] Another is ECFS standards of care on CFTR-related disorders: Updated diagnostic criteria. [15] Another is Molecular structures reveal synergistic rescue of Δ508 CFTR by Trikafta modulators. [20] Another is In vitro modulator responsiveness of 655 CFTR variants found in people with cystic fibrosis. [25] Related publications include PMID 28340353 [7]. Another is PMID 36207272 [13]. Another is PMID 36220763 [18]. Another is PMID 36264792 [23]. Another is PMID 38388235 [28]. One trial is Study of VX-809 in Cystic Fibrosis Subjects With the ∆F508-CFTR Gene Mutation [12]. Another is NPDT Evaluation in Children With CFTR and (PSC) [6]. Another is Detection of Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR) Activity in Rectal Tissues From Human Subjects [17]. Another is Effects of Sildenafil on CFTR-dependent Ion Transport Activity [22]. Another is Nasal Potential Studies Utilizing Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Regulator (CFTR) Modulators [27].
